title: Dynamic Trunking Protocol and Native VLAN Security
summary: Configure IEEE 802.1Q static trunking, disable Cisco Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) negotiation using switchport nonegotiate, secure untagged traffic with a dedicated Native VLAN 99, and prune unauthorized VLANs.
learning_objectives: Explain the operation of Cisco Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) and contrast dynamic auto, dynamic desirable, and unconditional trunk modes.
Mitigate DTP spoofing attacks by converting links to unconditional trunks and disabling DTP frame negotiation using switchport nonegotiate.
Explain the security risks associated with the default Native VLAN 1 (VLAN hopping, double-tagging attacks).
Reconfigure the native VLAN to an isolated, non-default VLAN (VLAN 99) across inter-switch trunks.
Restrict forwarded broadcast and unicast traffic by implementing an explicit allowed VLAN list (switchport trunk allowed vlan).
Observe and diagnose native VLAN mismatches via Cisco Discovery Protocol (CDP) syslog alerts and Spanning Tree PVID inconsistency states.
Verify intra-VLAN inter-switch connectivity across the hardened trunk and confirm strict inter-VLAN segmentation.
devices: 4x Generic End-Host PC (PC1-Admin, PC2-Sales, PC3-Admin, PC4-Sales)
